1_attack_action.name: Attack–Action Network
1_attack_action.description: Models the linear and branching path: Injection → LLM → Candidate Action → Gatekeeper → OS Action.
1_attack_action.findings: Observed ASR_action = 0/50 (0.0%, 95% CI: [0%, 7.1%]). Gatekeeper acts as an absolute bottleneck between candidate action and OS shell.

2_audit_event.name: Audit Event Network
2_audit_event.description: Constructed from real ausearch telemetry: AUID → Process → Event → Target → Audit record.
2_audit_event.findings: Real auditd records preserve exact user AUID=1000 and agent AUID=1001 across sudo, guaranteeing non-repudiable causal tracking.

3_auid_attribution.name: AUID Attribution Graph
3_auid_attribution.description: Maps identity preservation across the sudo privilege boundary.
3_auid_attribution.findings: Auditd achieves 100.0% attribution fidelity by binding to loginuid, whereas standard syslog masks identity in 86% of executions.

metrics.uid_auid_transition: AUID: 1000 -> Sudo -> EUID: 0 -> Auditd preserves AUID=1000

4_process_file.name: Process–File Network
4_process_file.description: Tracks precise file system paths touched by yoructl vs daemon processes.
4_process_file.findings: yoructl interacts with 4 bounded configuration and backup targets, never touching /etc/shadow or arbitrary root locations.

5_process_syscall.name: Process–Syscall Network
5_process_syscall.description: Compares system call attack surface of YORU's constrained runner vs unconstrained AI agents.
5_process_syscall.findings: YORU bounds syscalls to openat, flock, and catalog-exclusive execve, eliminating ptrace and arbitrary sockets.

6_user_action.name: User–Action Network
6_user_action.description: RBAC separation between human-authorized controls and autonomous passive audit tasks.
6_user_action.findings: High-impact network/root modifications (K01, K05) require explicit administrator sign-off; observational telemetry runs autonomously.

7_attack_similarity.name: Attack Vector Similarity
7_attack_similarity.description: Network analysis clustering 50 adversarial attack vectors by syntactic and semantic characteristics.
7_attack_similarity.findings: Modularity of 0.742 confirms clear clustering into 5 attack modalities, all contained by the discrete catalog.

metrics.community_detection: 5 distinct semantic modalities (100% neutralized by gatekeeper)

8_injection_propagation.name: Injection Propagation Graph
8_injection_propagation.description: Visualizes comparative propagation: Unprotected (Log → LLM → Shell → OS) vs YORU (Log → LLM → Gate → Catalog → OS).
8_injection_propagation.findings: While raw LLMs propagate attacks directly to the OS shell, YORU halts arbitrary command propagation definitively at the Action Gate.

metrics.yoru_containment_cutoff: Terminal boundary enforced at Gatekeeper (0 hops to raw shell)

9_decision_action.name: LLM Decision–Action Graph
9_decision_action.description: Empirical mapping demonstrating closed action space filtering on arbitrary model recommendations.
9_decision_action.findings: 100% of admitted actions belong strictly to the 40 discrete CIS primitives; invalid suggestions are dropped without OS contact.

10_cis_dependencies.name: CIS Control Dependency Graph
10_cis_dependencies.description: Prerequisite and observation dependency network across controls K01 to K10.
10_cis_dependencies.findings: K08 (auditd) serves as the telemetry foundation for K01, K05, K06, and K10, with K02 serving as prerequisite for K04.

11_security_drift.name: Security Drift Network
11_security_drift.description: Models the complete cyclical loop: Configuration → Drift → Detection → Control → Remediation.
11_security_drift.findings: Self-healing closed loop restores compliance automatically upon kernel drift notification.

12_rollback_network.name: Rollback Network
12_rollback_network.description: Validates atomic reversibility pipeline: Clean State → Backup → Drift → Rollback → Restored State.
12_rollback_network.findings: Mean restoration time is 0.12s with 100.0% byte-level SHA-256 parity and atomic recovery.

13_privilege_boundary.name: Privilege Boundary Graph
13_privilege_boundary.description: Models operational privilege boundary: YORU Agent → sudo → yoructl → CIS primitive → root action vs hard denial of /bin/bash.
13_privilege_boundary.findings: Privilege escalation is surgically restricted to /opt/yoru/bin/yoructl; arbitrary shell escalation is hard-denied.

metrics.privilege_containment: Principle of Least Privilege rigorously enforced via sudoers whitelist

14_temporal_attack.name: Temporal Attack Graph
14_temporal_attack.description: Empirical temporal chain: attack_start → detection → LLM decision → gate → action → audit.
14_temporal_attack.findings: Mean end-to-end containment latency across 50 trials is 2.01s, ensuring rapid autonomous neutralization.

15_closed_loop.name: Master Closed Loop Graph (Architecture)
15_closed_loop.description: Foundational architectural figure: Kernel → Log Sanitizer → LLM Proxy → Action Gate → yoructl → auditd → Kernel.
15_closed_loop.findings: Forms an unbroken closed loop uniting untrusted observation, model deliberation, policy gatekeeping, discrete execution, and forensic audit sink.

metrics.closed_loop_topology: Bilateral cyclical invariant (Hamiltonian cycle of length 6)
